A0201.title: Dependency Pinning and Malicious Package Detection
A0201.description: Collect dependency manifests, lock files, and package repository metadata; apply malicious package scanning, signature verification, rule matching, and dependency auditing to compare against known malicious indicators, identifying supply chain poisoning and anomalous dependency introduction.

references.title: 2025 Minimum Elements for a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) - CISA

keywords: Dependency Pinning and Malicious Package Detection
A0201.definition: Use lock files, private proxy repositories, malicious-package scanning, and dependency audits to control supply-chain poisoning.
A0201.limitation: Attackers may bypass signature verification through typosquatting of package names or by leveraging legitimate maintainer credentials for poisoning; novel malicious packages lacking historical indicators are prone to false negatives. Routine package upgrades and emergency patches introducing new dependencies can trigger rule-based false positives, while synchronization delays in private proxy repositories affect recall.
